summary.en: A fishing village where Ōta Dōkan built Edo Castle in 1457, Edo became the seat of the Tokugawa shoguns in 1603 and one of the world's largest cities. Renamed Tokyo ("eastern capital") in 1868, it became the imperial capital.
summary.zh: 原为渔村，1457年太田道灌在此修筑江户城。1603年起成为德川将军的驻地，并发展为世界最大城市之一。1868年改称东京（“东方之京”），成为天皇所在的首都。

sources.title: Conrad Totman, A History of Japan (Blackwell, 2nd ed. 2005)
Marius B. Jansen, The Making of Modern Japan (Harvard University Press, 2000)

summary.en: Founded by Emperor Kanmu in 794 as Heian-kyō on the model of Chang'an, Kyoto was the seat of the imperial court for over a thousand years and the centre of Japanese aristocratic and religious culture until the emperor moved to Tokyo.
summary.zh: 794年桓武天皇仿照长安建立平安京。此后一千多年里，京都一直是天皇朝廷所在地和日本贵族与宗教文化的中心，直至天皇移居东京。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Historic Monuments of Ancient Kyoto (Kyoto, Uji and Otsu Cities)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 2: Heian Japan (1999)

polity.zh: 朝鲜王朝 / 大韩帝国

summary.en: The Han River basin held Baekje's first capital and was fought over by the Three Kingdoms. Joseon made Hanseong its capital in 1394; under Japanese rule it was Keijō, and since 1945 it has been Seoul, capital of South Korea.
summary.zh: 汉江流域曾是百济最早的都城所在，并为三国反复争夺。1394年朝鲜王朝定都汉城；日本殖民时期称京城，1945年后称首尔（汉语旧称汉城），为韩国首都。

sources.title: Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
Ki-baik Lee, A New History of Korea (Harvard University Press, 1984)

note: Early Baekje dates follow the traditional Samguk sagi chronology; the "Namgyeong" designation dates from 1067.

summary.en: Capital of Silla for nearly a thousand years, Seorabeol was renamed Gyeongju by Goryeo after Silla's surrender in 935. Its royal tombs, temples and observatory make it an open-air museum of Silla culture.
summary.zh: 徐罗伐作为新罗都城近千年，935年新罗归降后被高丽改名为庆州。城内王陵、寺院与瞻星台使其成为新罗文化的露天博物馆。

sources.title: Kim Bu-sik, Samguk sagi (History of the Three Kingdoms, 1145)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Gyeongju Historic Areas

note: The 57 BCE founding date is traditional.

polity.zh: 唐安东都护府 / 边地
苏联民政局（苏联占领下的朝鲜北部）

polity.en: North Korea (Democratic People's Republic of Korea)
polity.zh: 朝鲜民主主义人民共和国

summary.en: Site of the Chinese Lelang commandery until 313, Pyongyang became Goguryeo's capital in 427. Goryeo made it the Western Capital, and since 1948 it has been the capital of North Korea.
summary.zh: 313年以前为中国乐浪郡治所，427年成为高句丽都城。高丽时期称西京，1948年起为朝鲜民主主义人民共和国首都。

sources.title: Kim Bu-sik, Samguk sagi (History of the Three Kingdoms, 1145)
Ki-baik Lee, A New History of Korea (Harvard University Press, 1984)

note: Lelang boundaries and dates before 313 are approximate. 1945–1948: seat of the Soviet Civil Administration and the Provisional People's Committee; the DPRK was proclaimed on 9 September 1948.

summary.en: Japan's first long-lasting capital, Heijō-kyō, was laid out here in 710. After the court left in 784, its great temples—Tōdai-ji, Kōfuku-ji, Kasuga shrine—kept Nara alive as the "southern capital" of Buddhism.
summary.zh: 日本第一座长期使用的都城平城京于710年在此兴建。784年朝廷迁离后，东大寺、兴福寺、春日大社等寺社使奈良作为佛教的“南都”延续繁荣。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Historic Monuments of Ancient Nara
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 1: Ancient Japan (1993)

summary.en: Wang Geon's home town of Songak became Gaegyeong, capital of Goryeo, for almost five centuries. Lying just south of the 38th parallel, it passed to North Korean control in the Korean War.
summary.zh: 王建的故乡松岳后来成为高丽都城开京，历时近五百年。开城位于三八线以南不远，在朝鲜战争中转归朝鲜控制。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Historic Monuments and Sites in Kaesong

note: Taebong used Songak as capital only c. 898–905.

summary.en: As Naniwa it was a port and intermittent capital from the 7th century. Hideyoshi built Osaka Castle on the site of the Ishiyama Hongan-ji, and under the Tokugawa the city became Japan's commercial "kitchen".
summary.zh: 古称难波，自7世纪起即为港口，并几度成为都城。丰臣秀吉在石山本愿寺旧址修建大坂城；德川时代这里发展为日本的商业中心，号称“天下的厨房”。

sources.title: The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 4: Early Modern Japan (1991)
Conrad Totman, A History of Japan (Blackwell, 2nd ed. 2005)

note: Naniwa served as capital only intermittently (645–655, 744–745); the 大坂→大阪 spelling change took place around 1868–1870.

summary.en: Minamoto no Yoritomo chose this coastal town, protected by hills, as his headquarters in 1180. It was Japan's political centre until the shogunate fell in 1333 and is known for the Great Buddha and Tsurugaoka Hachiman shrine.
summary.zh: 1180年源赖朝选择这座三面环山、一面临海的小城作为大本营。直到1333年幕府灭亡，这里一直是日本的政治中心，以镰仓大佛和鹤冈八幡宫闻名。

sources.title: Azuma kagami (Mirror of the East, late 13th c.)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 3: Medieval Japan (1990)

name.en: Shuri (royal capital) and the port of Naha

name.zh: 那霸（首里至1954年为独立市）

polity.en: US administration of the Ryukyu Islands
polity.zh: 美国管理下的琉球列岛

summary.en: Shuri, on the hills above the harbour of Naha, was the royal seat of the Ryukyu Kingdom from the 15th century until 1879. Naha became the capital of Okinawa Prefecture, was destroyed in the 1945 battle, served as the seat of US administration, and absorbed Shuri in 1954.
summary.zh: 位于那霸港上方丘陵的首里，从15世纪到1879年一直是琉球王国的王都。那霸后来成为冲绳县厅所在地，在1945年冲绳战役中被毁，战后是美国管理当局的驻地，1954年合并了首里。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Gusuku Sites and Related Properties of the Kingdom of Ryukyu
George H. Kerr, Okinawa: The History of an Island People (Tuttle, 1958; rev. 2000)

name.zh: 札幌（阿伊努人聚落地带）

polity.en: Ainu lands of Ezo, Matsumae trade sphere
polity.zh: 虾夷地阿伊努人地域（松前藩贸易范围）

polity.en: Empire of Japan (Kaitakushi seat, then Hokkaido government)
polity.zh: 大日本帝国（开拓使驻地，后为北海道厅）

summary.en: The name comes from Ainu, usually explained as "dry, great river". The Meiji Kaitakushi chose the Ishikari plain site in 1869 and laid out a grid city; Sapporo became the capital of Hokkaido and hosted the 1972 Winter Olympics.
summary.zh: 地名源于阿伊努语，一般解释为“干涸的大河”。1869年明治政府的开拓使选定石狩平原上的这一地点，按棋盘格规划城市；札幌后来成为北海道的首府，并举办了1972年冬季奥运会。

note: Ainu settlement long predates 1604; the first range starts with the Matsumae trade grant.

polity.en: Wajin forts of southern Ezo (Andō and Kakizaki)
polity.zh: 道南和人诸馆（安东氏、蛎崎氏）
松前藩及幕府箱馆奉行

summary.en: Known to the Ainu as Usukeshi, the bay got its Japanese name, traditionally from a box-shaped fort built about 1454. Opened to foreign ships by the 1854 Kanagawa treaty, it was the seat of the short-lived Republic of Ezo at the star fort Goryōkaku in 1868–69; its characters were changed from 箱館 to 函館 in 1869.
summary.zh: 阿伊努人称此地为宇须岸，相传约1454年有人在此修筑了形似箱子的馆，由此得到日语名称。1854年《神奈川条约》使其向外国船只开放；1868至1869年，短命的虾夷共和国以星形要塞五棱郭为据点；1869年其汉字写法由“箱馆”改为“函馆”。

polity.zh: 日本殖民统治下的朝鲜

polity.en: US military government, then Republic of Korea
polity.zh: 驻朝美军政厅，后属大韩民国

summary.en: Korea's great southern port. As Dongnae it guarded the coast facing Tsushima; under Joseon its waegwan was the only place Japanese traders could live. Opened by the 1876 treaty, it grew under Japanese rule and served as the wartime capital in 1950–53 when the Pusan Perimeter held.
summary.zh: 朝鲜半岛南部的大港。古称东莱，扼守面对对马岛的海岸；朝鲜王朝时，这里的倭馆是日本商人唯一可以居住的地方。1876年依条约开港，在日本殖民统治下迅速扩张，1950至1953年釜山防御圈守住时曾为战时首都。

sources.title: Kim Bu-sik, Samguk sagi (History of the Three Kingdoms, 1145)
Encyclopedia of Korean Culture (Academy of Korean Studies): Busan

note: Early dates are approximate; Geochilsan-gun was renamed Dongnae-gun in 757.

polity.zh: 日本殖民统治下的朝鲜

summary.en: Seoul's port on the Yellow Sea. Legend makes it Michuhol, the kingdom of Onjo's brother Biryu; it took the name Incheon in 1413, opened to foreign trade as Jemulpo in 1883, and was the site of MacArthur's amphibious landing in September 1950.
summary.zh: 首尔在黄海上的门户。传说这里是温祚之兄沸流所建的弥邹忽；1413年改称仁川，1883年以济物浦之名开港通商，1950年9月麦克阿瑟在此实施两栖登陆。

sources.title: Kim Bu-sik, Samguk sagi (History of the Three Kingdoms, 1145)
Encyclopedia of Korean Culture (Academy of Korean Studies): Incheon

note: The Michuhol founding is legendary; Goryeo-era names changed several times.

polity.en: Na, a Wa state, later Yamato

summary.en: The Book of Later Han records a gold seal sent in 57 CE to the King of Na of Wa, found on Shikanoshima in 1784. Its port Hakata was Japan's gateway to the continent and the Mongol landing site of 1274 and 1281; in 1601 Kuroda Nagamasa built Fukuoka Castle beside the merchant town, and the two merged as Fukuoka city in 1889.
summary.zh: 《后汉书》记载公元57年东汉赐倭奴国王金印，该印于1784年在志贺岛出土。其港口博多是日本通往大陆的门户，也是1274年和1281年蒙古军登陆之地；1601年黑田长政在商业町旁修筑福冈城，两地于1889年合并为福冈市。

sources.title: Fan Ye, Hou Hanshu (Book of the Later Han), Account of the Eastern Barbarians
Fukuoka City Museum: Gold Seal "King of Na of Wa"

polity.zh: 镰仓、室町、德川时代的日本

summary.en: Taira no Kiyomori rebuilt the harbour of Ōwada-no-tomari for trade with Song China and in 1180 briefly moved the capital to nearby Fukuhara. As Hyōgo it was a major medieval port; the treaty port opened in 1868 at the village of Kōbe grew into one of Japan's great cities.
summary.zh: 平清盛为与宋朝贸易而修整大轮田泊，1180年还一度把都城迁到附近的福原。中世纪时这里以“兵库津”之名成为重要港口；1868年在神户村开设的条约港，后来发展成日本的大城市之一。

note: Fukuhara served as capital for about six months in 1180.

polity.zh: 日本殖民统治下的朝鲜

summary.en: After Goguryeo took Hanseong in 475, Baekje moved its capital south to Ungjin on the Geum River. The intact tomb of King Muryeong (d. 523), found here in 1971, revealed close ties with Liang China and Japan. Renamed Gongju in 940, it was later the provincial capital of Chungcheong.
summary.zh: 475年高句丽攻陷汉城后，百济把都城南迁到锦江畔的熊津。1971年在此发现的武宁王（523年卒）陵完好无损，揭示了百济与南朝梁及日本的密切联系。940年改称公州，后来成为忠清道的首府。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Baekje Historic Areas
Kim Bu-sik, Samguk sagi (History of the Three Kingdoms, 1145)

polity.zh: 日本殖民统治下的朝鲜

summary.en: King Seong moved Baekje's court to Sabi in 538 and renamed the kingdom Nam-Buyeo. It fell to the Silla–Tang alliance in 660; legend says the palace women threw themselves from the Nakhwaam cliff into the Baengma River. Silla renamed the town Buyeo in 757.
summary.zh: 538年百济圣王迁都泗沘，并改国号为“南扶余”。660年泗沘被新罗与唐的联军攻陷；相传宫女们从落花岩投入白马江。757年新罗将其改名为扶余。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Baekje Historic Areas
Kim Bu-sik, Samguk sagi (History of the Three Kingdoms, 1145)
